details: The likelihood of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in September has increased to nearly 60%, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool. This comes after a surge in inflation and oil prices, attributed to the ongoing war with Iran. While the Fed opted to keep rates paused at its last five meetings in 2026, the July meeting saw an unusually divided vote with three regional Fed presidents favoring a quarter-point hike. Markets are now closely watching upcoming U.S. jobs data (August 7) and inflation reports (CPI on August 12, PPI on August 13) for further signals on the Fed's next moves.
title: Fed Rate Hike Prospects Rise Amid Inflation and Oil Price Surge

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revised down its global economic growth forecast for 2026 to 3%, a slight reduction from its 3.1% projection in April. The IMF attributes this adjustment to the persistent effects of the Middle East conflict and growing trade fragmentation, which continue to weigh on the global economy. Global inflation is now expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026. Despite the challenging outlook, the IMF notes that AI-driven demand is partially offsetting some of the economic impact, and anticipates a recovery to 3.4% growth in 2027.
title: IMF Lowers Global Growth Forecast for 2026, Citing Geopolitical Risks

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council decided to keep its three key interest rates unchanged at its meeting on July 23, 2026, with the deposit facility rate remaining at 2.25%. The ECB acknowledged that uncertainty stemming from ongoing wars and trade frictions continues to impede Eurozone economic growth, which is projected at 1% for 2026. However, the central bank highlighted that a significant shift in business investment towards intangible assets like Artificial Intelligence (AI) is helping to mitigate this economic drag. Inflation, excluding energy and food, showed a slight easing to 2.4%.
title: ECB Holds Rates Steady Amid Eurozone Uncertainty, AI Mitigates Drag

details: Easing geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran have reportedly led to a reduction in risk premiums across financial markets and a decline in inflation expectations. This positive shift contributed to a broader strengthening of risk assets, including technology and semiconductor stocks. Progress in negotiations concerning the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz has also pushed oil prices sharply lower, further supporting this sentiment.
title: US-Iran Tensions Ease, Boosting Risk Assets and Lowering Inflation Bets

details: The landscape for U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ethereum Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) presents a mixed picture. Recent reports indicate significant daily net inflows, with U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recording $211 million and Ethereum ETFs seeing $53.7 million in total net inflows on August 4th, 2026, with BlackRock's IBIT and ETHA leading the way. However, other analyses point to cautious institutional behavior, with U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs experiencing a $61.5 million outflow last week, ending a three-week streak of inflows. Furthermore, Hashdex's DEFI ETF has reportedly closed due to dwindling inflows, with investors rotating into AI-focused funds. Meanwhile, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a crucial piece of U.S. crypto regulation, remains stalled in the Senate, with the probability of its passage in 2026 dropping to a historic low of around 37%.
title: US Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs See Mixed Flows, CLARITY Act Stalls
